items: This constructor sets default values upon object creation without requiring any arguments.

rows: Has no parameters. Initializes object with default values.
Takes arguments to initialize the object with specific values.

items: If no constructor is provided, Java provides a default constructor.
If any constructor is defined, Java does not provide a default constructor.
Constructors can be overloaded (multiple constructors with different parameter lists).
Constructors do not have return types.
✅ Use constructors to initialize mandatory fields of an object.
✅ Avoid using setters for fields that should not change after object creation.
✅ Helps in creating immutable objects when paired with final variables.
Ensures object consistency from the start.
Helps prevent errors like null fields.
Encourages encapsulation by setting values only once during instantiation.
